activity_context.topic_title: Writing Sums of Trigonometric Functions in Amplitude-Phase Form

feedback.problem:
Express $2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+7\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ in the form $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ)$ with $ϕ\in (0,\frac{\pi }{2}).$ Use the **exact value** for $R,$ and round $ϕ$ to **three decimal places**.

$2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+7\operatorname{cos}⁡x≈$
{{field-1}}
$\operatorname{sin}⁡(x\,+$
{{field-2}}$)$
feedback.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+7\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+7\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & =(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=7\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{7}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{7}{2} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{7}{2}) \\ ϕ & ≈1.292\,\text{rad},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡(ϕ)+{R}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡(ϕ) & ={7}^{2}+{2}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡(ϕ)+{cos}^{2}⁡(ϕ)) & =49+4 \\ {R}^{2} & =53 \\ R & =\sqrt{53}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+7\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)≈\sqrt{53}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+1.292)
$$
